title: Advanced Financial Accounting
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 400L Advanced Financial Accounting curriculum building on ACC201/301 financial accounting: consolidated financial statements, business combinations, accounting for associates and joint arrangements, foreign currency translation, liquidation and reconstruction, and IFRS-based group reporting (IFRS 3, 10, 11, IAS 21, 27, 28, 33).

questions.question: Under IFRS 3, what is the accounting term for the excess of the consideration transferred in a business combination over the acquirer's share of the net identifiable assets acquired?
options: Goodwill
Bargain purchase gain
Non-controlling interest
Retained earnings
questions.correct_answer: Goodwill
questions.explanation: IFRS 3 defines goodwill as the excess of the consideration transferred (plus NCI and any previously held interest) over the net fair value of identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed.

questions.question: A parent company owns 80% of a subsidiary's ordinary shares. In the consolidated statement of financial position, how should the parent treat the subsidiary's assets and liabilities?
options: Consolidate 100% of the subsidiary's assets and liabilities, then recognise a non-controlling interest for the 20%
Consolidate only 80% of the subsidiary's assets and liabilities
Show the investment in the subsidiary at cost using the equity method
Exclude the subsidiary entirely and disclose it only in the notes
questions.correct_answer: Consolidate 100% of the subsidiary's assets and liabilities, then recognise a non-controlling interest for the 20%
questions.explanation: IFRS 10 requires full (line-by-line) consolidation of a controlled subsidiary's assets and liabilities regardless of the percentage owned, with the non-controlling shareholders' interest shown separately in equity.

questions.question: Under IFRS 10, control over an investee is presumed to exist when the investor has all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A 25% non-voting preference shareholding with no board representation
Power over the investee
Exposure or rights to variable returns from involvement with the investee
The ability to use its power to affect the amount of the investor's returns
questions.correct_answer: A 25% non-voting preference shareholding with no board representation
questions.explanation: Control under IFRS 10 requires power, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use power to affect those returns; a passive non-voting preference holding with no board influence gives none of these.

questions.question: How is non-controlling interest (NCI) measured at acquisition under the 'full goodwill' (fair value) method permitted by IFRS 3?
options: At the NCI's proportionate share of the fair value of identifiable net assets
At the fair value of the NCI's shareholding, which may include goodwill attributable to the NCI
At the NCI's share of the subsidiary's book value only
NCI is never recognised under IFRS 3
questions.correct_answer: At the fair value of the NCI's shareholding, which may include goodwill attributable to the NCI
questions.explanation: IFRS 3 allows an acquirer to elect, on an acquisition-by-acquisition basis, to measure NCI at fair value (full goodwill method) or at its proportionate share of identifiable net assets (partial goodwill method).

questions.question: Parent P acquired 75% of Subsidiary S for N9,000,000 when S's identifiable net assets had a fair value of N10,000,000. Using the partial (proportionate) goodwill method, what is goodwill on acquisition?
questions.explanation: Goodwill = Consideration transferred - (75% x fair value of identifiable net assets) = N9,000,000 - (75% x N10,000,000) = N9,000,000 - N7,500,000 = N1,500,000.

questions.question: Which financial reporting standard prescribes the accounting treatment for investments in associates using the equity method?
options: IAS 28
IAS 21
IFRS 8
IAS 33
questions.correct_answer: IAS 28
questions.explanation: IAS 28 'Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures' requires the equity method to be applied to associates over which the investor has significant influence.

questions.question: Under the equity method, how does an investor's carrying amount for an investment in an associate change during the year?
options: It remains fixed at original cost throughout the holding period
It is increased or decreased by the investor's share of the associate's post-acquisition profit or loss, and reduced by dividends received
It is revalued to fair value through profit or loss every year like a trading investment
It is written off immediately to retained earnings on acquisition
questions.correct_answer: It is increased or decreased by the investor's share of the associate's post-acquisition profit or loss, and reduced by dividends received
questions.explanation: Under the equity method, the investment is initially recognised at cost and subsequently adjusted for the investor's share of the associate's post-acquisition profit/loss, less dividends received.

questions.question: A holding of 20% to 50% of the voting power of an investee is generally presumed, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, to give the investor:
options: Control
Significant influence
Joint control
No influence
questions.correct_answer: Significant influence
questions.explanation: IAS 28 presumes significant influence (but not control) where an investor holds 20%-50% of the voting power of the investee.

questions.question: Under IFRS 11, a joint arrangement in which the parties have rights to the net assets of the arrangement (rather than direct rights to assets and obligations for liabilities) is classified as a:
options: Joint operation
Joint venture
Subsidiary
Associate
questions.correct_answer: Joint venture
questions.explanation: IFRS 11 distinguishes joint operations (rights to assets, obligations for liabilities) from joint ventures (rights to net assets only), with joint ventures accounted for using the equity method.

questions.question: On consolidation, unrealised profit on inventory sold by a parent to its subsidiary and still held at year end must be:
options: Ignored because the sale is legally complete
Eliminated from consolidated retained earnings and from the value of closing inventory
Added to consolidated goodwill
Recognised in full as it increases group profit
questions.correct_answer: Eliminated from consolidated retained earnings and from the value of closing inventory
questions.explanation: From the group's perspective, profit is not earned until sale to an external party, so unrealised profit on intra-group inventory still on hand must be eliminated (provision for unrealised profit, PUP).

questions.question: Subsidiary S sold goods to its parent P for N800,000, including a mark-up of 25% on cost. If P still holds all these goods in inventory at year end, what is the unrealised profit to be eliminated?
questions.explanation: Mark-up of 25% on cost means profit = 25/125 x selling price = 25/125 x N800,000 = N160,000.

questions.question: Where the unrealised profit on intra-group sales originates from the SUBSIDIARY (the 'downstream/upstream' distinction), how is the provision for unrealised profit allocated for NCI purposes?
options: It is always charged wholly to the parent's retained earnings
It is shared between the parent and NCI in the group's ownership ratio, since it reduces the subsidiary's own recorded profit
It is ignored for NCI computation
It is added entirely to NCI
questions.correct_answer: It is shared between the parent and NCI in the group's ownership ratio, since it reduces the subsidiary's own recorded profit
questions.explanation: When the selling company is the subsidiary (upstream sale), the unrealised profit adjustment reduces the subsidiary's profit for the year, so it must be split proportionately between parent and NCI.

questions.question: In preparing a consolidated statement of financial position, intra-group balances such as a payable in the subsidiary matched by a receivable in the parent must be:
options: Grossed up and shown separately
Cancelled (eliminated) against each other on consolidation
Reported as a contingent liability
Transferred to goodwill
questions.correct_answer: Cancelled (eliminated) against each other on consolidation
questions.explanation: Intra-group receivables and payables represent amounts owed within the single economic entity and must be eliminated on consolidation to avoid overstating group assets and liabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'pre-acquisition profits' of a subsidiary in consolidation?
options: Profits earned by the subsidiary after the date the parent gained control
Profits earned by the subsidiary before the date the parent gained control, which are capitalised (not treated as group distributable profit)
Profits the parent earned before acquiring the subsidiary
Dividends paid by the parent
questions.correct_answer: Profits earned by the subsidiary before the date the parent gained control, which are capitalised (not treated as group distributable profit)
questions.explanation: Pre-acquisition retained earnings existed before the parent obtained control and are included in the net assets acquired (affecting goodwill), not treated as post-acquisition group profit.

questions.question: IAS 21 requires that, on consolidation, the assets and liabilities of a foreign subsidiary be translated into the presentation currency at:
options: The historical rate at the date of acquisition
The closing rate at the reporting date
The average rate for the year
The rate ruling when each individual transaction occurred
questions.correct_answer: The closing rate at the reporting date
questions.explanation: Under IAS 21, assets and liabilities of a foreign operation are translated at the closing rate, while income and expenses are generally translated at rates approximating the exchange rate on transaction dates (often the average rate).

questions.question: Under IAS 21, exchange differences arising on translating the financial statements of a foreign operation are recognised in:
options: Profit or loss immediately
Other comprehensive income, accumulated in a separate component of equity (foreign currency translation reserve)
Retained earnings directly, bypassing profit or loss and OCI
Goodwill
questions.correct_answer: Other comprehensive income, accumulated in a separate component of equity (foreign currency translation reserve)
questions.explanation: IAS 21 requires translation differences on consolidating a foreign operation to be recognised in OCI and accumulated in a separate equity component until disposal of the foreign operation.

questions.question: A Nigerian company has a foreign currency receivable. At year end, if the naira has depreciated against the foreign currency since the transaction date, the retranslation of that monetary receivable will generally result in:
options: An exchange loss
An exchange gain
No exchange difference
A reduction in share capital
questions.correct_answer: An exchange gain
questions.explanation: If the naira weakens, each unit of foreign currency is now worth more naira, so a foreign-currency receivable translates to a higher naira amount, producing an exchange gain.

questions.question: In company liquidation, what is a 'Statement of Affairs' primarily used for?
options: To record daily cash transactions of a solvent company
To show the estimated realisable value of assets and the amounts due to various classes of creditors and shareholders on winding up
To compute annual depreciation charges
To prepare the statement of cash flows
questions.correct_answer: To show the estimated realisable value of assets and the amounts due to various classes of creditors and shareholders on winding up
questions.explanation: The Statement of Affairs is prepared in a liquidation to present estimated asset realisations against liabilities, ranked by priority of payment, showing the expected deficiency or surplus.

questions.question: Under company liquidation law, which of the following ranks as a 'preferential creditor' typically paid before ordinary unsecured creditors?
options: Ordinary trade suppliers
Employees' unpaid wages/salaries (up to statutory limits)
Ordinary shareholders
Debenture holders secured by a floating charge (paid after preferential creditors from that charge's proceeds)
questions.correct_answer: Employees' unpaid wages/salaries (up to statutory limits)
questions.explanation: Employees' wages and certain statutory dues rank as preferential debts, paid ahead of unsecured creditors and ahead of amounts secured only by a floating charge.

questions.question: The 'Deficiency Account' prepared in a liquidation is designed to explain:
options: The movement in inventory during the year
How the company's capital and profits have been lost, reconciling the shareholders' funds at the last balance sheet date to the deficiency now shown
The company's tax computation
The bank reconciliation
questions.correct_answer: How the company's capital and profits have been lost, reconciling the shareholders' funds at the last balance sheet date to the deficiency now shown
questions.explanation: The Deficiency (or Surplus) Account reconciles the last balance sheet's net assets/capital position to the estimated deficiency/surplus at liquidation, explaining losses, since the earlier date.

questions.question: Internal reconstruction of a company (e.g. capital reduction scheme) is primarily undertaken to:
options: Wind up the company and distribute assets to shareholders
Eliminate accumulated losses and restate the balance sheet on a sound basis without liquidating the company
Merge with another unrelated company
Increase the company's authorised share capital only for expansion
questions.correct_answer: Eliminate accumulated losses and restate the balance sheet on a sound basis without liquidating the company
questions.explanation: Internal reconstruction (e.g. via a capital reduction or scheme of arrangement) writes off accumulated losses and overvalued assets against share capital/reserves, allowing the company to continue trading with a clean balance sheet.

questions.question: In amalgamation accounted for as an 'amalgamation in the nature of a merger' (pooling of interests), assets and liabilities of the transferor company are generally recorded in the transferee's books at:
options: Fair value with resulting goodwill
Their existing book values, with no goodwill arising
Net realisable value
Zero, as they are written off
questions.correct_answer: Their existing book values, with no goodwill arising
questions.explanation: A merger-type amalgamation (pooling of interests) carries forward the book values of assets, liabilities, and reserves rather than restating to fair value, so no goodwill or capital reserve typically arises purely from the combination.

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes 'absorption' from 'amalgamation' in company reconstruction?
options: In absorption, an existing company takes over one or more other companies which are then dissolved; in amalgamation, two or more companies combine to form a new company
There is no difference between the two terms
Absorption always involves liquidation of the acquiring company
Amalgamation only applies to public companies
questions.correct_answer: In absorption, an existing company takes over one or more other companies which are then dissolved; in amalgamation, two or more companies combine to form a new company
questions.explanation: In absorption, one existing company (the transferee) absorbs another which ceases to exist; in amalgamation, two or more companies are dissolved and a brand new company is formed to take them over.

questions.question: IAS 33 requires disclosure of basic earnings per share, computed as:
options: Total assets divided by number of shares outstanding
Profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders of the parent divided by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period
Dividend paid divided by market price per share
Net profit divided by total equity
questions.correct_answer: Profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders of the parent divided by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period
questions.explanation: IAS 33 defines basic EPS as profit/loss attributable to ordinary shareholders of the parent, divided by the weighted average number of ordinary shares in issue during the period.

questions.question: When computing diluted earnings per share under IAS 33, which of the following is treated as a potential ordinary share that may dilute EPS?
options: Redeemable preference shares classified as a financial liability
Convertible bonds that can be converted into ordinary shares
Trade payables
Bank overdraft
questions.correct_answer: Convertible bonds that can be converted into ordinary shares
questions.explanation: Convertible instruments (bonds, convertible preference shares, share options/warrants) are potential ordinary shares; their conversion is assumed for diluted EPS if the effect would reduce EPS (i.e., is dilutive).

questions.question: A company has profit attributable to ordinary shareholders of N15,000,000 and a weighted average of 5,000,000 ordinary shares in issue during the year. What is the basic EPS?
questions.explanation: Basic EPS = N15,000,000 / 5,000,000 shares = N3.00 per share.

questions.question: Under IFRS 8, an operating segment is reportable separately if its reported revenue (including intersegment sales) is what percentage or more of total combined revenue of all operating segments?
questions.explanation: IFRS 8 sets the quantitative threshold at 10% of combined revenue, reported profit/loss, or assets for a segment to be separately reportable.

questions.question: Under IFRS 16, a lessee is generally required to recognise, for almost all leases, a:
options: Right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability on the statement of financial position
Simple rental expense only, with no balance sheet recognition
Contingent asset only
Deferred tax asset equal to the full lease payments
questions.correct_answer: Right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability on the statement of financial position
questions.explanation: IFRS 16 largely eliminated the operating/finance lease distinction for lessees, requiring recognition of a right-of-use asset and lease liability for almost all leases (subject to short-term/low-value exemptions).

questions.question: Under IFRS 9, which category of financial asset is measured at fair value through other comprehensive income (with recycling to profit or loss on derecognition) for debt instruments?
options: Assets held solely to collect contractual cash flows

Assets held within a business model whose objective is achieved by both collecting contractual cash flows and selling financial assets, with cash flows that are solely payments of principal and interest
Assets held for trading only
Equity investments designated at FVTPL
questions.correct_answer: Assets held within a business model whose objective is achieved by both collecting contractual cash flows and selling financial assets, with cash flows that are solely payments of principal and interest
questions.explanation: IFRS 9 classifies debt instruments as FVOCI when held under a 'hold to collect and sell' business model and cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest (SPPI test), unlike amortised cost ('hold to collect' only).

questions.question: Which financial statement is specifically required by IAS 7 to report an entity's cash receipts and payments classified into operating, investing, and financing activities?
options: Statement of changes in equity
Statement of cash flows
Statement of comprehensive income
Statement of financial position
questions.correct_answer: Statement of cash flows
questions.explanation: IAS 7 governs the statement of cash flows, requiring cash flows to be classified into operating, investing, and financing activities.

questions.question: In a consolidated statement of cash flows, dividends paid by a subsidiary to its non-controlling interest shareholders are classified as:
options: An operating cash outflow
A financing cash outflow of the group
An investing cash inflow
Not shown at all because NCI is outside the group
questions.correct_answer: A financing cash outflow of the group
questions.explanation: Dividends paid to NCI represent a distribution to the group's non-controlling equity holders and are shown as a financing activity outflow in the consolidated cash flow statement.

questions.question: A Value Added Statement, commonly presented as supplementary information by Nigerian companies, primarily shows:
options: The wealth created by the enterprise (value added) and how it is distributed among employees, government, providers of capital, and retained for reinvestment
The company's tax computation for the Federal Inland Revenue Service
A simple restatement of the statement of financial position
The company's break-even point
questions.correct_answer: The wealth created by the enterprise (value added) and how it is distributed among employees, government, providers of capital, and retained for reinvestment
questions.explanation: The Value Added Statement, a socially-oriented disclosure common in Nigerian corporate reporting, reconciles revenue less bought-in materials/services to value added, then shows its distribution to stakeholders.

questions.question: Under defined benefit pension accounting (IAS 19), actuarial gains and losses (remeasurements) on the net defined benefit liability/asset are recognised in:
options: Profit or loss immediately
Other comprehensive income, and are not subsequently reclassified to profit or loss
Share capital directly
They are never recognised
questions.correct_answer: Other comprehensive income, and are not subsequently reclassified to profit or loss
questions.explanation: IAS 19 (revised) requires remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability/asset, including actuarial gains and losses, to be recognised in OCI and not recycled to profit or loss in later periods.

questions.question: Where a parent disposes of part of its interest in a subsidiary but retains control, IFRS 10 requires the transaction to be accounted for as:
options: A disposal that generates a gain or loss on the parent's investment
An equity transaction between the parent and the NCI, with no gain or loss recognised in profit or loss
A step acquisition requiring goodwill remeasurement
Discontinuation of consolidation
questions.correct_answer: An equity transaction between the parent and the NCI, with no gain or loss recognised in profit or loss
questions.explanation: IFRS 10 treats changes in a parent's ownership interest that do not result in loss of control as transactions with owners in their capacity as owners (equity transactions), so no gain/loss is recognised.

questions.question: When a parent loses control of a subsidiary (full disposal), IFRS 10 requires any retained investment to be remeasured at:
options: Its original historical cost
Fair value at the date control is lost, with the difference included in the gain/loss on disposal
Zero
The subsidiary's book value of net assets
questions.correct_answer: Fair value at the date control is lost, with the difference included in the gain/loss on disposal
questions.explanation: On loss of control, IFRS 10 requires derecognition of the former subsidiary's assets/liabilities and NCI, and any retained interest is remeasured to fair value, with the resulting gain or loss recognised in profit or loss.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the conditions IFRS 10 lists as evidence of an investor having power over an investee?
options: Voting rights giving the investor the current ability to direct relevant activities
Potential voting rights that are currently exercisable or convertible
The investor's physical head office being located in the same city as the investee
Contractual arrangements giving the investor decision-making rights
questions.correct_answer: The investor's physical head office being located in the same city as the investee
questions.explanation: Geographic proximity of head offices is irrelevant to control assessment; IFRS 10 focuses on voting rights, potential voting rights, and contractual arrangements that confer decision-making power over relevant activities.

questions.question: In a step acquisition where a parent already held a 15% equity investment before acquiring a further 65% to gain control, IFRS 3 requires the previously held 15% interest to be:
options: Ignored in the goodwill calculation
Remeasured to fair value at the acquisition date, with any resulting gain or loss recognised in profit or loss, and included as part of the consideration for goodwill purposes
Kept at its original cost with no remeasurement
Written off to reserves without passing through profit or loss
questions.correct_answer: Remeasured to fair value at the acquisition date, with any resulting gain or loss recognised in profit or loss, and included as part of the consideration for goodwill purposes
questions.explanation: IFRS 3 treats a business combination achieved in stages by requiring the acquirer to remeasure its previously held equity interest to acquisition-date fair value through profit or loss, and to include that fair value in the goodwill calculation.
